The actual defect this revision exists to fix -- src/app/components/NotificationsCard.tsx:47-48's `const subscribed = (await getCurrentDeviceEndpoint()) !== null; dispatch({type: 'loaded', ...})`, which awaits the hangable/rejectable subscription lookup BEFORE dispatching any state -- has no assertion anywhere in this suite. An implementer can satisfy every assertion here by loosening `subscribed` to optional on the type while leaving NotificationsCard.tsx's load() ordering byte-for-byte unchanged (the field is simply omitted from the object passed to dispatch, still built after the same await), which would compile, pass all 25 runtime tests, and leave the hang defect this revision documents completely intact. This is a strict subset of the AC-9 defect-fix delta's required observable property: the type must PERMIT omitting subscribed, AND the component must actually dispatch 'loaded' without waiting on the subscription-check promise -- only the first half is asserted. Closing assertion: extract load()'s two-step sequence into a pure, DOM-free orchestrator in src/shared (e.g. a function taking an injected `() => Promise<boolean>` subscription-check port, mirroring this project's own 'extract the decidable part behind a port' rule in docs/context/methodology.md), and assert -- using a manually-deferred/never-resolving promise for that port -- that the 'loaded' event for blocked/explainer/enabled is produced/dispatched before the injected promise ever settles. That is an assertion on await ORDERING, not on type shape, and cannot be satisfied by a type edit alone.
